<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920519_theRebbe_475" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920519_theRebbe_475__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section raises questions about the joy of judgment on Rosh Hashanah, the paradox of a close relative being unfit to judge, and the specific term "tevel" in the verse.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, it is brought in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="2">on the verse</t>
    <t s="3">"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day," it says,</t>
    <t s="4">"Let the field exult and all that is in it,"</t>
    <t s="5">"Let the field exult" — this is the world, etc.,</t>
    <t s="6">"And all that is in it" — these are the creatures, etc.,</t>
    <t s="7">Before Whom?</t>
    <t s="8">Before Hashem,</t>
    <t s="9">Why?</t>
    <t s="10">For He comes on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="11">What to do?</t>
    <t s="12">"He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity."</t>
    <t s="13">And it is necessary to understand: what is the joy of "Let the field exult and all that is in it" from the judgment?</t>
    <t s="14">Is this not [a matter of] law and judgment?</t>
    <t s="15">And superficially, it would be better without any judgment at all.</t>
    <t s="16">And even more perplexing,</t>
    <t s="17">for our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="18">that even if the entire world tells you that you are righteous, be in your own eyes like a wicked person,</t>
    <t s="19">and our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="20">three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="21">the completely righteous are immediately inscribed for life,</t>
    <t s="22">the completely wicked, etc.,</t>
    <t s="23">and if so,</t>
    <t s="24">how is it possible to be in a state of joy?</t>
    <t s="25">Also, it is necessary to understand,</t>
    <t s="26">is it not written</t>
    <t s="27">"For the judgment is for God,"</t>
    <t s="28">and regarding the children of Israel it is said</t>
    <t s="29">"For whom God is close to him,"</t>
    <t s="30">as it is written</t>
    <t s="31">"You are children to Hashem your God,"</t>
    <t s="32">and it is written</t>
    <t s="33">"For the sake of my brothers and companions,"</t>
    <t s="34">and behold, a relative is disqualified to judge.</t>
    <t s="35">And also, it is necessary to understand what is said: "He will judge the world with righteousness,"</t>
    <t s="36">what is the matter of "with righteousness,"</t>
    <t s="37">and what is the precise language of "tevel" specifically.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the seventh of everything is beloved, and the seventh name of the land, "tevel," is the most beloved, which is why the verse specifies "tevel."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">But the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">for behold, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="2">"All sevenths are beloved,"</t>
    <t s="3">In days, the seventh is beloved,</t>
    <t s="4">the day of Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="5">as it is said</t>
    <t s="6">"And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it"</t>
    <t s="7">(and our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="8">He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with manna,</t>
    <t s="9">and likewise our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="10">He sanctified it with the light of a person's face,</t>
    <t s="11">for the light of a person's face on a weekday is not comparable to the light of a person's face on Shabbat),</t>
    <t s="12">In months, the seventh is beloved,</t>
    <t s="13">the seventh month,</t>
    <t s="14">which is satiated with everything, for it is blessed in physicality and spirituality,</t>
    <t s="15">as our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="16">"winepresses within it, blessings within it,"</t>
    <t s="17">for it is the time of the harvest,</t>
    <t s="18">and likewise in spirituality,</t>
    <t s="19">for it contains many mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="20">Shofar, Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkah, the Four Species, and Shemini Atzeres.</t>
    <t s="21">Therefore, also in the land, the seventh is beloved,</t>
    <t s="22">for just as there are seven firmaments,</t>
    <t s="23">Shamayim, Shmei HaShamayim, Rakia, Shechakim, Zevul, Maon, and Aravos,</t>
    <t s="24">and it is written</t>
    <t s="25">"Pave [a way] for Him who rides through the plains, by Yah is His name,"</t>
    <t s="26">meaning,</t>
    <t s="27">that Aravos, which is the seventh, is the beloved,</t>
    <t s="28">because in it are found the souls of the righteous, etc.,</t>
    <t s="29">and therefore it is beloved to the Holy One, blessed be He, to ride upon them,</t>
    <t s="30">so too is it in the land,</t>
    <t s="31">which has seven names,</t>
    <t s="32">Eretz, Adamah, Arka, Gai, Tziyah, Neshiyah, Tevel,</t>
    <t s="33">behold, Tevel, which is the seventh, is the beloved,</t>
    <t s="34">and concerning this it is said "He will judge the world (tevel) with righteousness,"</t>
    <t s="35">specifically tevel.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that judgment relates to the service of Torah, prayer, and charity, and that the two aspects of "tzedek" (righteousness) correspond to bounded charity and unbounded charity.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand this, it is necessary first to preface the matter of judgment,</t>
    <t s="2">which is regarding the entirety of the service of the past year in the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="3">in all three lines of Torah, service, and acts of kindness,</t>
    <t s="4">which are the three things upon which the world stands,</t>
    <t s="5">the totality of which is the matter of tzedakah (charity/righteousness).</t>
    <t s="6">For behold,</t>
    <t s="7">even Torah is a matter of tzedakah,</t>
    <t s="8">for Torah, in its own essence, is beyond comparison, etc.,</t>
    <t s="9">and its drawing down into the world is a matter of tzedakah.</t>
    <t s="10">And this connection</t>
    <t s="11">(that the Torah is drawn down into the world)</t>
    <t s="12">is effected by the souls of the Jewish people through their service,</t>
    <t s="13">and this is,</t>
    <t s="14">because the thought of Israel preceded even the thought of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="15">And likewise, service,</t>
    <t s="16">which is the matter of the service of the offerings,</t>
    <t s="17">and in this time it is the matter of prayer,</t>
    <t s="18">behold, it is connected with tzedakah,</t>
    <t s="19">as our Sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="20">Rabbi Elazar would give a coin to a poor person and then pray,</t>
    <t s="21">as it is said</t>
    <t s="22">"I, through righteousness (tzedek), shall behold Your face."</t>
    <t s="23">And this is,</t>
    <t s="24">that through tzedakah, there is achieved in prayer the matter of "beholding Your face,"</t>
    <t s="25">specifically "Your face,"</t>
    <t s="26">the aspect of the innerness of Elokus that is revealed through the innerness of the soul,</t>
    <t s="27">and therefore prayer is upon [the name] Havayah</t>
    <t s="28">(and Channah prayed upon Havayah),</t>
    <t s="29">above the name Havayah.</t>
    <t s="30">And this is what is said: "He will judge the world (tevel) with righteousness (tzedek),"</t>
    <t s="31">two [instances of] tzedek,</t>
    <t s="32">which are two aspects of tzedek,</t>
    <t s="33">the aspect of tzedek that is in acts of kindness and prayer,</t>
    <t s="34">which is the matter of tzedakah within limitation,</t>
    <t s="35">and the aspect of tzedek that is in Torah,</t>
    <t s="36">which is the matter of tzedakah without limitation.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
